Path.write_text emits CRLF on Windows. Any test about line endings that uses it compares CRLF against CRLF and passes against the defect - use write_bytes. Cost one round in F73.

A duplicate-evidence test needs the second run's workspace_dir set to a checkout of the same commit, or the two footprints name different shas, no duplicate is possible, and the test passes against the defect. Cost one round in F75.

To enumerate what a Python module actually emits, parse the BALANCED call expression at each `persist_event(`/`record_event(` and pull the event_type literal plus the payload keys - a plain grep misses every site whose payload is built in a variable above the call, which was three of F105's ten. `summaryForEvent` is reached ONLY from EventRow.tsx and LogLine.tsx, both reading event_logs, so a broadcast-only kind reaches no timeline and is not a candidate.

GET /projects/{id}/questions filters on `answered` (a bool), NOT `status`. FastAPI silently discards an unrecognised query parameter, so `?status=pending` returns EVERYTHING and reads like a filter that matched. The answer route is PATCH /questions/{id} with {"answer": ...}; POST /questions/{id}/answer is a 405 and /decline is the only POST sub-route.

There is no GET /projects/{id}/runs/{run_id} -- it hangs/404s. Read a run's outcome straight from the sqlite `runs` table (status, exit_code, ended_at, pid, workspace_dir) and its trace from `agent_outputs` ordered by `sequence` (kinds: tool_use, tool_result, text). That is the fastest ground truth for any drive, and `messages` will be empty for an operator-triggered turn.
